summary: ITERATION 4 — MongoDB→MySQL migration verified. 34/34 backend tests pass (4 new migration tests + 30 existing). MySQL is confirmed as the live store (`GET /api/` -> version 2.0, db MySQL), DB auto-bootstraps EMPTY on startup, analytics returns all zeros pre-seed, POST /api/seed wipes-and-recreates 3 demo users + 8 potholes deterministically, data persists across a `supervisorctl restart backend` (proves it's real MySQL not in-memory), duplicate detection within 20m works on lat/lng range query, upvote idempotency works on JSON-encoded `upvoted_by` text column, and WS /api/ws still broadcasts pothole_created / status_updated / upvoted on the respective MySQL mutations.

minor.issue: Legacy MONGO_URL and DB_NAME keys still present alongside DATABASE_URL. Harmless (unused after migration) but should be cleaned up to avoid confusion.

action_items: (Optional) Remove obsolete MONGO_URL / DB_NAME keys from /app/backend/.env now that MySQL is the sole store.
(Optional) Drop the unused `JSON` import in server.py — it is imported from sqlalchemy but never used (`upvoted_by` is stored as Text).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py cleanly migrated to SQLAlchemy 2.0 async + aiomysql; models, schemas, and routes are well-structured (~550 lines).
`Base.metadata.create_all` on startup handles fresh-DB bootstrap correctly — verified by empty-state analytics test.
Seed endpoint is properly idempotent: deletes status_updates -> potholes -> users (FK-safe order) then re-inserts.
Duplicate detection uses lat/lng ±0.0002 bounding box (~22m) — works correctly on MySQL indexed columns.
Upvote stores voter IDs as JSON text in `upvoted_by` column; idempotency confirmed via double-POST test.
WebSocket broadcasts fire AFTER `session.commit()` for create/status/upvote — correct ordering, no risk of broadcasting un-persisted state.
Pothole `assigned_to` is set to the staff user that performs the status->assigned transition — sensible behaviour.
Minor: `JSON` is imported from sqlalchemy but never referenced (upvoted_by uses Text). Safe to remove.
